clue.text: Revolving column of cloud that takes the rain away

definitions.meaning: a whirling funnel of cloud and spray over the sea
a pipe or gutter outlet carrying rainwater off a roof

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a marine whirlwind funnel and a gutter outlet that drains a roof.

clue.text: Avoids bias with vote that's free

indicators.note: set free, the letters are loosed from their order and rearranged

explanation.surface: A voter dodges prejudice by casting a free, independent ballot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the two fodder words and 'that's' links to the indicator 'free'.
explanation.definitionFit: To obviate is to prevent or get round a difficulty, a formal synonym of avoids.

clue.text: Spread the rest around two points

indicators.note: turned around, the letters of the word are moved into a new order

parts.note: W and N are two compass points, west and north

explanation.surface: Someone spreads the remainder about between two places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' is the anagram signal on the clue word 'rest'; 'the' is a link, and the two points are compass bearings.
explanation.definitionFit: Strewn is a past participle meaning scattered or spread about, matching spread used as a participle.

clue.text: Moored fleet

explanation.definitionFit: Fast means both firmly fixed (a boat made fast) and rapid, so it fits both senses.

clue.text: Features of wild scenery portrayed in Brontë novel

parts.note: a heath is an open moorland, one feature of wild country
a cliff is a steep rock face, another wild landscape feature

explanation.surface: A novel by a Brontë sister depicts the features of untamed moorland.
explanation.walkthrough: One phrase supplies two pieces: two features of wild scenery, the moor and the rock face. The character is the brooding hero of Emily Brontë's Wuthering Heights.
explanation.definitionFit: The definition points to the figure depicted in the novel, its central character of that name.

clue.text: He's paid to mind someone else's business

definitions.text: He's paid to mind someone else's business

parts.words: He's paid to mind someone else's business
parts.note: minding another's business sounds like nosiness, but here it is guarding someone's premises for a wage

explanation.definitionFit: A guard paid to look after a firm's premises minds, that is watches over, another's business.

clue.text: Open an eye?

parts.note: not an eye opening from sleep but the eye of a hook-and-eye fastening on clothing being undone

explanation.definitionFit: Releasing a hook from its eye is to unfasten it, opening the hook-and-eye clasp.

clue.text: Musical character to have on the staff

definitions.text: Musical character to have on the staff

parts.words: Musical character to have on the staff
parts.note: the staff is the five-line stave of written music, and the character is the symbol placed at its start

explanation.definitionFit: A clef is the symbol written on a musical stave that fixes the pitch of its lines.

clue.text: Bar attire set by judge

indicators.note: set in a new order, the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A barrister's courtroom outfit is laid out by the judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' is the anagram signal on BAR ATTIRE; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To arbitrate is to judge a dispute between parties, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Article left out of yearbook creates void

indicators.note: this phrase signals that the article is removed from the yearbook

parts.note: an annual is a book published once a year
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Omitting a piece from the yearbook leaves an empty gap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left out of' takes one A from ANNUAL.
explanation.definitionFit: To annul a contract or marriage is to declare it void, so the word creates voidness.

clue.text: It's apparent I've been set back by depression

indicators.note: set back means the word I've is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: I've written without its apostrophe
a dent is a small hollow or depression

explanation.surface: Clearly someone has been dragged down by gloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set back' turns the letters of I've round; 'It's' and 'by' are links. 'depression' suggests gloom but means a hollow.
explanation.definitionFit: Evident and apparent are synonyms: plain to see or obvious.

clue.text: Reprimand means no further credit will be given

definitions.meaning: to scold or tell someone off

definitions.text: means no further credit will be given
definitions.meaning: tick is informal British for credit, and with it off there is no more buying on tick

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to scold, while read literally it says credit on tick is stopped.

clue.text: First job-finder for the unemployed

parts.note: the proverb says the devil finds work for idle hands, so he was the original finder of work for the idle

explanation.definitionFit: The proverb holds that the devil finds work for idle hands, making him the first employment agent.

clue.text: He sets the rate, of course

definitions.text: He sets the rate, of course

parts.words: He sets the rate, of course
parts.note: 'of course' seems to mean naturally, but it means on a racecourse, where a runner sets the speed

explanation.definitionFit: A runner or rider who sets the speed of a race for others is called this.

clue.text: Revolutionary support for a key performer

definitions.text: Revolutionary support for a key performer

parts.words: Revolutionary support for a key performer
parts.note: revolutionary means spinning round, as an adjustable seat does, and the key performer plays a keyboard

explanation.definitionFit: The adjustable seat used by a pianist screws round to change height, so it revolves.

clue.text: Fatted calf was just the ticket for the prodigal son

definitions.text: Fatted calf was just the ticket for the prodigal son

parts.words: Fatted calf was just the ticket for the prodigal son
parts.note: in the parable the father killed the fatted calf for the son coming home, the meal he got on his way back

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a ticket price for travel home, and here also the feast awaiting a returner.

clue.text: A military point of view

parts.note: not an army opinion but a literal spot from which soldiers keep watch

explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers watch the enemy from such a position, a place literally giving a view.

clue.text: Smuggled wines and rifles

parts.note: to run goods is to smuggle them, past tense ran
sack is an old name for dry white wine such as sherry

explanation.surface: Contraband wine and guns are carried by smugglers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rifles' is not guns but a verb: searches roughly.
explanation.definitionFit: To rifle a place is to search and rob it, the same as ransacking it.

clue.text: Musical show high spot for a worker

parts.note: an opera is a staged musical drama
a tor is a rocky hilltop, especially on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: A highlight of a musical production suits a stagehand.
explanation.definitionFit: An operator is someone who works a machine, so a type of worker.

clue.text: Sending up from the runway?

parts.note: sending up means mocking, but read literally it is an aircraft rising off a runway

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both mimicking someone mockingly and an aeroplane leaving the ground.

clue.text: Illegally take trick, all the tricks

parts.note: to kid is to trick or tease
in the card game nap, going nap is bidding to win all five tricks

explanation.surface: A card player cheats by grabbing a trick and then every trick.
explanation.walkthrough: Nap is a British card game in which a bid of nap means winning every trick.
explanation.definitionFit: To kidnap is to seize and carry off a person unlawfully.

clue.text: Empty vault

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to empty or remove the contents
to jump over an obstacle without touching it

explanation.definitionFit: To clear a table is to empty it, and to clear a fence is to vault it.

clue.text: Twin helps in moving furniture

definitions.meaning: one of the heavenly twins, the brother of Pollux in Greek myth
a small swivelling wheel fitted under a chair or table leg

explanation.definitionFit: Castor is a mythological twin and also the swivel wheel on furniture legs.

clue.text: Lad lost at sea may profit from his advice

definitions.text: Lad lost at sea may profit from his advice

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled up

explanation.surface: A boy adrift on the ocean would do well to heed a veteran sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a boy lost on the ocean would do well to listen to an experienced seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: An experienced sailor is just the person a lost young seaman would learn from.

clue.text: A classic feature of English woods

definitions.meaning: one of the five English classic horse races, run at Epsom for fillies

explanation.definitionFit: The Oaks is an English classic horse race at Epsom, and oak trees fill English woods.

clue.text: Woman's work for girl employees

parts.note: Di is a short girl's name
the staff are the employees of a firm

explanation.surface: A firm's female workers take on the women's jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: Hand spinning, done with a stick called this, was traditionally women's work, hence the distaff side of a family.
explanation.definitionFit: The distaff is the spinning staff, and by extension women's work or concerns.

clue.text: Boiled sweet that's no good

definitions.meaning: a pudding boiled in a cloth
British slang for worthless or useless

explanation.definitionFit: A plum duff is a boiled pudding, and duff is British slang for useless.

clue.text: Without a second thought, pack a gift

indicators.note: without means these letters are dropped from the pack

parts.note: a knapsack is a pack carried on the back
PS, a postscript, is an afterthought added to a letter

explanation.surface: Someone hastily wraps up a present without thinking twice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' removes P and S, then A, from KNAPSACK.
explanation.definitionFit: A knack is a natural aptitude or talent, so a gift.

clue.text: A shade less well than usual

definitions.text: A shade less well than usual

parts.words: A shade less well than usual
parts.note: a shade means a little, and also hints at a colour that is wrong

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means slightly unwell, and literally describes a hue that is wrong.
